rule: Every conversion surface inherits this reviewed authority set through its classificationBatch. Canonical target specs and confirmed decision-log entries define redesigned behavior; current-product specs describe shipped behavior or constraints only; architecture and conversion-control documents own technical obligations, not product policy.

batches.title: App shell, shared presentation, and test support
batches.rationale: Presentation and test surfaces must render and exercise the redesigned accounting, Item, Client, Transfer, receipt-line, security, and offline contracts without preserving Firebase mechanics.

batches.title: Firebase Auth, account membership, invites, and MCP OAuth
batches.rationale: Identity, membership, invite, and MCP principal surfaces support authoritative Client relationships and approved offline/security behavior.

batches.title: Firebase Cloud Functions and privileged side effects
batches.rationale: Existing privileged side effects span every redesigned accounting writer and are source evidence only; target behavior comes from the canonical target specs.

batches.title: Firestore paths, dynamic data, and query/index boundary
batches.rationale: Firestore paths and rules reveal current entity and authorization boundaries, but target tables, RLS, and Sync Streams must enforce the redesigned product model.

batches.title: Firebase Storage, media references, thumbnails, and pending uploads
batches.rationale: Media references and upload durability support the unified Item flow and accounting evidence while target object policy remains private and offline durable.

batches.title: Capability evolution guidance and complete service/MCP surface catalog
batches.rationale: Coverage tooling governs how source and target obligations are tracked; it does not define product behavior.

batches.title: Hard-cutover source freeze and late-writer recovery control
batches.rationale: The final source freeze, late-writer recovery, and hard cutover are migration controls; they must preserve approved target behavior without implementing it in Firebase.

batches.title: Identity, account session, and operation lifecycle dossier surfaces
batches.rationale: Account selection, authorization, logout, and operation durability are reconciled with the new Client identity model and offline-access requirements.

batches.title: Inventory provenance, Transactions, receipts, and corrections
batches.rationale: Inventory, money, provenance, correction, and receipt surfaces are governed by the new story-specific accounting and Item lifecycle specs, not legacy movement Transaction mechanics.

batches.title: Invoicing, collection, and budget authority
batches.rationale: Invoice, collection, source membership, Expense/Fee, and budget surfaces are governed by the invoice-centered model and the related Item/receipt lifecycle.

batches.title: Unified Item creation, accounting Link, and legacy capture
batches.rationale: All current Item/proto creation surfaces are reconciled with the one-Item target wizard, accounting Link, occurrence, Invoice, and receipt-line model.

batches.title: Media, attachments, and offline byte durability dossier surfaces
batches.rationale: Attachment and offline-byte surfaces preserve media-heavy field workflows for the real-Item target and accounting evidence while changing storage mechanics.

batches.title: Platform, transport, release, and migration control
batches.rationale: Environment, transport, release, observability, and migration tooling implement architecture and operational controls; product behavior remains delegated to the owning domain batches.

batches.title: Projects, Clients, settings, and reference-data boundary dossier surfaces
batches.rationale: Project, Client, category, note, preference, and shared-reference surfaces are reconciled with authoritative Client identity and the redesigned accounting/budget boundary.

batches.title: Firestore query contract and fail-closed source profiling tools
batches.rationale: Query extraction and production shape profiling prove source behavior and migration completeness; they do not establish target product semantics.

batches.title: Reporting, search, and cross-domain projections
batches.rationale: Reports, search, exports, and cross-domain projections must consume the redesigned accounting/Item/Client authorities and preserve only approved report/search outcomes.

batches.title: Deterministic M2 residual decision-queue control
batches.rationale: Residual generation ensures every unmapped target surface remains tied to an explicit product, architecture, spike, or production-evidence blocker.

batches.title: Spaces, review, and work queues
batches.rationale: Space, assignment, review, and work-queue behavior is governed by the Space/Item specs and must remain compatible with the new one-Item provenance and accounting lifecycle.
